;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Manbij bombing]]
**In [[Manbij]], [[Syria]], a [[suicide attack]] claimed by [[Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] causes at least 19 casualties. Among them, two [[United States Army|U.S.]] soldiers, a Pentagon Civilian, and a civilian contractor are reported dead and three other Service Members injured. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/middle_east/blast-rocks-us-patrolled-city-in-syria-monitoring-group-local-media-report-casualties/2019/01/16/aefe0e78-1986-11e9-a804-c35766b9f234_story.html?utm_term=.79251f74e909 (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[2019 Nairobi attack]]
**Dozens of people remain missing one day after a deadly attack on a popular hotel complex in Nairobi, according to the Kenya Red Cross Society. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/kenya-s-leader-says-militants-who-attacked-nairobi-hotel-complex-n959191 (NBC News)]
*Gunmen attack two [[Village|villages]] in the [[Ménaka]] region, [[Mali]], near the border with [[Niger]], killing at least 20 people. [https://www.cas.sk/clanok/791552/mali-utok-ozbrojencov-na-dve-dediny-si-vyziadal-najmenej-20-mrtvych/ (NOVÝ CAS)]
*[[Second Libyan Civil War]]
**Five people are killed and twenty are injured in clashes between rival militias in [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]], breaking several months of relative peace. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/Libya-Tripoli-renewed-clashes-rival-militias-dead-235730700 (''Middle East Eye'')]
*[[Terrorism in the United States]]
**A man from [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] planned to attack the [[White House]] and even tried to trade his own car for weapons for the attack. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-46908505 (BBC News)]
;Law and crime
*At least 21 people are killed in a massacre by gunmen in police uniforms in [[Port-au-Prince]], [[Haiti]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/haiti-massacre-port-au-prince-police-uniforms-gangs-united-nations-a8729876.html (''The Independent'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[United States federal government shutdown of 2018–2019|United States federal government shutdown]]
**About 42,000 active-duty [[United States Coast Guard|Coast Guard]] members, who continue to work on essential operations, missed their scheduled paycheck Tuesday. This is the first time that [[United States Armed Forces]] servicemembers  have not been paid during a shutdown or other lapse in government appropriation. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/42-000-coast-guard-members-miss-first-paycheck-due-government-n958616 (NBC News)]
**President [[Donald Trump]] signs a bill which requires the government to compensate government employees after the shutdown is over for their work during the shutdown. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/01/16/politics/trump-signs-backpay-bill-government-shutdown/index.html?no-st=1547802883 (CNN)]
**[[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|Speaker of the House]] [[Nancy Pelosi]] suggests that [[President Trump]]'s [[State of the Union]] address [[2019 State of the Union Address|scheduled for January 29]] be delayed or use a drastically modified format due to security concerns related to the ongoing government shutdown. [https://www.npr.org/2019/01/16/685814372/pelosi-calls-for-postponement-of-state-of-the-union-address-due-to-shutdown (NPR)]
*[[Brexit negotiations]], [[Meaningful vote]]
**[[Theresa May]]'s government survives a [[2019 motion of no confidence in the May ministry|no confidence vote]] by a majority of 19. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-46899466 (BBC News)]
*[[2018 Andalusian regional election]]
**The [[Parliament of Andalusia|Andalusian parliament]] elects [[Juan Manuel Moreno Bonilla]] as the next [[President of the Regional Government of Andalusia|regional President]] with the votes of conservative party [[People's Party of Andalusia|PP]], liberal party [[Ciudadanos|Cs]] and far-right party [[Vox (Spanish political party)|Vox]], ending a 36-year term, since the restoration of democracy, of social democratic [[PSOE]] government. [https://www.elmundo.es/andalucia/2019/01/16/5c3f54a0fdddff6e438b4579.html (''El Mundo'')]
*[[Macedonia naming dispute]]
**[[Prime Minister of Greece|Greek Prime Minister]] [[Alexis Tsipras]] survives a no-confidence vote after the [[Independent Greeks]] party quit the ruling coalition. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/01/16/world/europe/greece-tsipras-confidence-vote.html (''The New York Times'')]
